rounds.text: ACC Ltd (ACC) appears to be under-appreciated based on the evidence provided. The company trades at a P/E ratio of 13.2x, which is significantly lower than the sector benchmark of 9.23x, indicating that ACC's stock price might be undervalued relative to its earnings growth potential. Additionally, ACC's Price-to-Book (P/B) ratio of 1.25x is also below the sector median of 1.64x, suggesting that the company may have a stronger balance sheet than its peers. Furthermore, ACC's Return on Assets (ROA) of 6.93% outperforms the sector benchmark of -11.63%, implying efficient asset utilization and potentially higher profitability. The compounded profit growth over three years is 33%, which is significantly higher than both the five-year and ten-year compound profit growth rates, indicating strong recent performance that has not yet been reflected in the stock price. The discounted cash flow (DCF) analysis suggests an intrinsic value of Rs 1998 per share against a market price of Rs 1357, leaving a margin of safety of 32.1%. This further supports the argument that ACC is undervalued. Moreover, the Fundamental-led signal from scanX indicates that profit growth has outpaced stock price declines over the past five years, suggesting that the company's fundamentals are currently outpacing its market performance. The recent screen reasons (bull side) for earnings growth accelerating and a DCF margin of safety of 32% also support this view. While ACC is trading at a slight premium to its historical range by 15%, it remains within a reasonable band, and the sector median profit growth rate of 11.5% suggests that ACC's performance could be even better than expected in the future. Therefore, based on these evidence points, ACC Ltd appears to be under-appreciated given its current valuation relative to both historical and projected fundamentals.
